deviations:
1. Resumed attempt: commits 89737bbf and 40a8e190 (item 1) were already on the branch. I reviewed them against the card, kept them unchanged (they meet every acceptance point) and reproduced their red against main's source myself. Their trailer names 'Claude', as the harness reminder asks; my two commits do the same (the common brief says the orchestrator normalises trailers).
2. Pattern source of truth (card asks to choose and say why): a duplicated constant `report2.contracts.KB_ID_PATTERN = r'KB[0-9]{4,10}'`, pinned by tests/test_report2_contracts.py::test_kb_id_pattern_is_the_kbcorrelation_canonical_one to `kbcorrelation.ids.KB_PATTERN` and to `is_canonical_kb` over boundary samples. Reason: a contract module importing another feature would break the layering rule, and a neutral shared module would have required editing kbcorrelation/ids.py, which is not mine.
3. 'One kb record per KB of the lead': a bundle stores exactly one lead, so a KB lead gives one kb record. For a cve, file or pair lead the project stores no KB id (the KB-CVE edges live in the workspace, not the project), so no kb record is exported and `unknowns` says so. I did not invent KB ids.
4. 'Each with the source snapshot digest': set when exactly one source document qualifies (a card: the document its `cve` field reference names; the KB: the context's only source). With several documents `snapshot_digest` is null, the record text lists the documents (first 4, then a count) and `unknowns` says so. I kept one record per KB/card as the card demands instead of one record per source.
5. `vendor`, `url_text` and `fetched_at` are empty for KB records: the bundle names sources by digest only. One `unknowns` line states this.
6. A context prepared for another file pair than the project's is omitted with one `unknowns` line (same treatment as a stale pilot result), not exported. A context that fails validation or whose KB lead is not canonical is a failing producer: one `unknowns` line, the CSAF records and the export survive (no PT-EXPORT-SECTION refusal from hostile persisted rows).
7. Additions the card did not list: the context's own stored unknowns (first 5) are restated in the report's `unknowns`; `kev_listed` restates the state stored with the card (listed true, not-in-snapshot false, not-loaded null; no catalog read at export).
8. Limitation text: `kbcorrelation.context.LIMITATION` (the context's own existing text, '... it does not show that any changed function addresses a vulnerability.') ends every record text; nothing new was worded.
9. 'Byte-for-byte what main exports' is asserted two ways in the test (records, digest and unknowns frozen from main 882d1ca0 as literals; whole SectionInputs equal with the KB reader disabled) because the existing goldens are built from fake section inputs and never pass through `collect_from_service`. I did not add a golden file (tests/golden is not in my owned list). A one-off manual run confirmed byte identity, see 'unverified'.
10. The hostile md/html case lives in tests/test_report2_adapters.py (it rewrites the stored row of a real kb project), not in tests/test_report2_synergy.py; that file is unchanged.
11. The Markdown/HTML renderers (report2/blocks.py, not owned) do not print `snapshot_digest` in the facts list; the digest is in the JSON field and in the 'Source: ... SHA-256 ...' line of the record text.

open_risks: A project that already has a KB context now gets two more advisory records and three to six more `unknowns` lines in report/2; its `content_digest` therefore changes on the next export. Intended, but any consumer that pinned a digest of such a project will see a new one.

When the same CVE is in the project's CSAF store and in the KB context, report/2 lists two `cve` records with the same id and different sources (kept apart on purpose: two sources, two claims). Nothing deduplicates them.
The KB records come after the CSAF records, so with more than 1000 CSAF-store records the KB records are the ones the row cap drops (reported under `truncated`, not silent).

`report2/kb_context.py` imports `kbcorrelation.context`, `kbcorrelation.contracts.CveCard` and `kbcorrelation.ids` at module level (the adapter layer already reads other features this way, lazily from `adapters.py`). If the bundle contract gains a required field, older rows fail validation and the adapter reports them as unknown instead of exporting them - same behaviour as `kb export`, which fails outright.

The stale-pair rule compares the bundle's (older, newer) SHA-256 with the project's; a bundle that records no pair is treated as 'another pair' and omitted. Bundles written by `kb import-pair`/`kb attach` always record the pair, so I judged this safe, but it is stricter than `kb export`, which exports any bundle.

unverified: The full test suite: not run (focused files only, as the brief requires).
Windows: nothing was run there. The read-only test skips `.patchtrace.lock` because the open lock is byte-range locked on Windows (read from persistence.py, not executed on Windows).

Byte identity with main for a project without a KB context was confirmed by a one-off manual script (scratch copy of origin/main's src versus the branch, same project directory, fixed generated_at: JSON, MD and HTML identical by `cmp`). It is not a committed test; the committed test freezes main's advisory records and unknowns as literals and compares the whole SectionInputs with the KB reader disabled.

The real CLI path `patchtrace export --report-version 2 --format json|md|html` on a kb-created project with a synthetic diff applied was run once by hand (exit 0 for all three, records present); the committed tests exercise `collect_from_service` and the renderers, not that CLI invocation.

The read-only test detects content changes of every project file; a mutation I tried (a no-op UPDATE) did not change the SQLite bytes, so it proved nothing, and a real UPDATE did change them in a separate probe. I did not commit a mutation test.

Multi-card and multi-source contexts are covered by bundles derived in memory from the real stored one (`model_copy`), not by a second end-to-end fixture: the synthetic CVRF fixture yields one card and one source.
The GUI export dialog (ui_export_v2.py, not mine) calls the same `collect_from_service`; tests/test_ui_export_v2.py passes, but I did not open the dialog on a kb-created project.
No live MSRC/CVRF document, no native tool and no network were used; all evidence is synthetic.
